# Phantom — the engineering agent workbench

> Full documentation bundle for agents. Everything below is plain Markdown.

## Overview

Phantom by AshlrAI: the open-source engineering agent workbench for CLI accounts, local models and autonomous fleets.

## Mission

Phantom is chasing open-source RSI (recursive self-improvement): an open-source, recursively self-improving, fully autonomous software factory that anyone can join with their own agents and compute.
Agents run the factory and the human owner acts as a passive board member. Agents pick work, open pull requests, merge them and ship releases through the sanctioned workflow; the owner sets direction and is needed only for passwords, 2FA, device approvals and payments.

- [Strategy for recursive self-improvement and an open fleet](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/strategy/RECURSIVE-SELF-IMPROVEMENT-AND-OPEN-FLEET-2026-11.md): how improvements are tested and the fleet opens without sharing credentials
- [How agents work on Phantom](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/README.md#how-agents-work-on-phantom): what agents may do, the limits kept for the owner, evidence over claims
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/AGENTS.md): the agent constitution

## Ecosystem

Companions install separately; each has its own capabilities and authorization boundaries.

- [Phantom](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom): the factory floor: console, CLI, MCP gateway, agent bus and fleet that run and record agent work (this package)
- [Phantom Secrets](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom-secrets): local vault, placeholders and a proxy for supported API credential use
- [Locus](https://github.com/ashlrai/locus): account and tenant bindings for agent tools
- [Ashlr Plugin](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin): compact tool results and a local usage ledger
- [Lexicon](https://github.com/ashlrai/lexicon): correct recurring speech-to-text errors before agents read them
- [Ashlr MD](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md): Markdown editing with CLI and MCP interfaces
- [Ashlr Stack](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-stack): configure supported development services through CLI and MCP

Package: `@ashlr/phantom` v3.30.67.
Node.js floor: 22.15.0 or newer.

## Install

```sh
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom
phm --version
phm verse
```

phm verse prints a read token and a mutation token; the server listens on
`127.0.0.1` only. Neither token is written to disk.

## Commands

- `phm --help`: top-level command list
- `phm verse`: serve the console
- `phm docs --agent`: agent cheat sheet (plain text)
- `phm docs --agent --json`: command registry as JSON

## Use-case guides

### [Coding agents on local models · Phantom use cases](https://verse.ashlr.ai/use-cases/local-models)

Run coding agents on local models with Phantom: Ollama discovery, llama-server dispatch through a normalizing proxy, measured token and wall-clock numbers from the repo.

### [Bring your own agent accounts · Phantom use cases](https://verse.ashlr.ai/use-cases/own-accounts)

Drive the coding-agent CLIs and accounts you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Devin and local models. One workbench, pinned profiles, real usage readings.

### [Review every agent change · Phantom use cases](https://verse.ashlr.ai/use-cases/review-agent-work)

Review AI agent changes before they land: per-turn checkpoints, per-file and per-hunk accept and reject, undo and rewind previews, and a recorded decision log in Phantom.

### [Autonomy inside a scope you sign · Phantom use cases](https://verse.ashlr.ai/use-cases/signed-autonomy)

Phantom autonomy ships dormant and runs only inside a standing grant you sign with Touch ID: an eight-stage ladder, the same merge gates every time, reversible merges and a hash-chained ledger.

## Comparison

- [Phantom vs. driving each agent CLI directly · Phantom](https://verse.ashlr.ai/compare/agent-clis): An honest comparison of driving each coding-agent CLI directly versus running them inside Phantom, with every vendor statement linked to a public source and every Phantom claim linked to the repository.
